text:
Alex K: noticed a big uptick in console chart freezes starting ~09:10 UTC during the canary rollout for prefetch-router v2. charts hang for ~3-6s, main thread pegged. graph: https://grafana.internal/r/console/chart-lcp?from=now-30m :eyes:
Maria P: same here. CPU spikes on the browser-side telemetry client in canary, not the server. timeline aligns with the rollout.
Sam R: weird — prefetch-router v2 only changed route selection heuristics + added telemetry event for routing-decisions. did we accidentally increase payload sizes?
Jordan L: I pulled a recording from a user session and saw massive telemetry batches being enqueued: payloads ~200-300KB per batch, coming every ~5s.
Alex K: repro steps I used: repro-app -> open dashboard with 8 charts -> apply time range -> observe freeze. I can share HAR if helpful.
Maria P: HAR would help. I also captured console logs:
```
telemetryClient.enqueue({type: 'route-decision', ctx: {..., fullModelPerf: {...}}})
// fullModelPerf contains a 150KB structured trace object
```
Sam R: ohhh. fullModelPerf should be sampled out for client telemetry. looks like a regression in telemetry-sampler (we bumped sampling config in the router rollout).
Ben (deploy-bot): deploy: canary prefetch-router v2 -> 2026-03-19T09:05:13Z (20% traffic)
Claire T: Quick idea: throttle telemetry batching + cap individual event size client-side to 8KB until we fix. That should prevent main-thread stringify/parse stalls.
Jordan L: Agree. On canary instances I toggled TELEMETRY_MAX_EVENT_SIZE=8192 and saw median chart freeze drop from 3.8s -> 0.7s in the sampled session. Not a full fix but huge improvement.
Alex K: Nice. Who can ship a hotfix? We should either revert the telemetry change in prefetch-router or add client-side caps + sampling change.
Sam R: I can push a quick client patch with size cap + drop heavy fields. small patch:
```
// in telemetry-client
const capped = truncateEvent(event, TELEMETRY_MAX_EVENT_SIZE)
queue.push(capped)
```
Sam R: will open a PR in 10m.
Maria P: also adding a guard in router: do not attach fullModelPerf to client events unless DEBUG flag.
Claire T: We should also update rollout checklist: any new telemetry fields must be reviewed for size impact. Maybe add a perf test that serializes synthetic events and measures stringify time.
Jordan L: good call. I can add a lightweight benchmark to perf-tests repo.
Ben (deploy-bot): action required: rollback toggle available at https://deploys.internal/rollbacks/prefetch-router-v2
Alex K: For immediate mitigation — Sam, please do the client cap PR. Maria, can you open a quick router revert patch if Sam's fix doesn't land in 30m?
Maria P: will prepare a revert PR as standby.
Sam R: PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4821 — implements TELEMETRY_MAX_EVENT_SIZE env var and truncation. cc @MariaP
Alex K: testing now on canary — patch applied to a subset via feature flag. monitoring dashboard shows freeze rate down ~70% after 5m. great work. :tada:
Claire T: follow-ups: (1) add spec for telemetry event size in the README, (2) perf test for stringify time, (3) rollout gating that checks client-side median freeze before increasing canary.
Jordan L: I'll own the perf test. Claire, can you take the gating addition?
Claire T: yes.
Alex K: tagging product: @eng-product — this was a telemetry instrumentation regression during a routing rollout, not a chart rendering change. we need postmortem note and better rollout checks.
Maria P: leaving logs and HARs in #eng-platform/attachments for postmortem.
Ben (deploy-bot): deploy: prefetch-router v2 rollback started by Maria P at 2026-03-19T09:28:00Z
Alex K: thanks everyone. after rollback we'll schedule a short postmortem and add the gating + perf tests before we attempt v2 again.
